short: Lost Normandy, taxed England hard, and was forced to seal Magna Carta.
full:
John succeeded his brother Richard I in 1199 and lost the heart of the Angevin inheritance within five years: Philip Augustus overran Normandy, Anjou and most of Poitou by 1204. Recovering them dominated the rest of the reign and required money, which John raised through scutage, arbitrary reliefs, forest fines and the manipulation of debts owed to the crown.

His quarrel with Innocent III over the appointment of Stephen Langton to Canterbury brought a six-year interdict and John's own excommunication, ended only when he made England a papal fief in 1213. The campaign he had paid for collapsed with his allies' defeat at Bouvines in 1214, and his barons rebelled. At Runnymede in June 1215 he agreed to the charter that became Magna Carta; both sides repudiated it within months. John died at Newark in October 1216 in the middle of a French invasion, leaving a nine-year-old heir and a kingdom at war.
